title: Standard charts and coordinate sections of projective space over a scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $n$ a finite nonempty index set, $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_k:k\in n])$ with $\deg T_k=1$, and $P=\mathbf P(n;S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with first projection $q:P\to S$ and second projection $\rho:P\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$. Let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the twisting sheaf of $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] with its global sections $T_k$, put $\mathcal O_P(1)=\rho^*\mathcal O(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and write $T_k$ also for the pulled-back sections in $\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$. For $i\in n$ let $D_+(T_i)\subseteq\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ be the standard open [def-nagata-affine-proj], $D_+(T_i)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[T_j/T_i:j\in n]$, put $D_+(T_i)_S=\rho^{-1}(D_+(T_i))$ and, for $j\in n$, $u_{j/i}=\rho^*(T_j/T_i)\in\Gamma(D_+(T_i)_S,\mathcal O_P)$. Then: (a) $P=\bigcup_{i\in n}D_+(T_i)_S$; (b) for every morphism of schemes $g:Y\to P$ and every $i,j\in n$, the section $g^*T_i$ of the invertible module $g^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-sc-invertible-module] is a free generator of $g^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ over $g^{-1}(D_+(T_i)_S)$ (every section over an open $V\subseteq g^{-1}(D_+(T_i)_S)$ is $a\cdot g^*T_i$ for exactly one $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$), and $g^*T_j=g^*(u_{j/i})\cdot g^*T_i$ on $g^{-1}(D_+(T_i)_S)$; in particular ($g=\mathrm{id}_P$) the open set $P_{T_i}$ where $T_i$ does not vanish (its image in $\mathcal O_P(1)_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ is nonzero) is $D_+(T_i)_S$; (c) for every affine open $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and every $i\in n$, the open $D_+(T_i)_S\cap q^{-1}(S')$ is affine and the $R$-algebra map $R[U_j:j\in n\setminus\{i\}]\to\Gamma(D_+(T_i)_S\cap q^{-1}(S'),\mathcal O_P)$, $U_j\mapsto u_{j/i}$, from the polynomial ring is an isomorphism.

proof.text: *The two descriptions of $\mathcal O(1)$.* The statement takes $\mathcal O(1)$ to be the glued module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] (with $A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$) with the global sections $T_k$ whose restriction to $D_+(T_i)$ is $(T_k/T_i)e_i$; [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] works with $\widetilde{S(1)}$, $S=\mathbf Z[T_k:k\in n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twist-glued-identification] there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O$-modules $\theta:\mathcal O(1)\to\widetilde{S(1)}$ with $\theta(T_k)=T_k$ for all $k$. For any morphism $h:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, $h^*\theta:h^*\mathcal O(1)\to h^*\widetilde{S(1)}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules ($h^*$ is a functor [def-pc-module-pullback]) and $h^*\theta(h^*T_k)=h^*T_k$ (naturality of the unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to h_*h^*$: $h_*h^*\theta\circ\eta=\eta\circ\theta$). An isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules carries free generators over an open to free generators, relations $t=a\,s$ to the same relations, and, on stalks, $\mathfrak m_y$-multiples to $\mathfrak m_y$-multiples, so it preserves non-vanishing loci. Hence every assertion of (b) holds for $\mathcal O(1)$ iff it holds for $\widetilde{S(1)}$ (apply this with $h=\rho\circ g$, and use the identification $g^*\rho^*\cong(\rho g)^*$ of step 3, which is natural in the module). From now on $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ with its sections $T_k$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts]. (This is the identification of the two descriptions recorded in the ledger on 2026-10-09.)

*(a).* The homogeneous elements $T_i$ ($i\in n$) generate the irrelevant ideal $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ of $S=\mathbf Z[T_k:k\in n]$: a homogeneous polynomial of positive degree is a $\mathbf Z$-linear combination of monomials of positive degree, each divisible by some $T_i$. By the cover clause of [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\bigcup_{i\in n}D_+(T_i)$. Taking preimages under the continuous map $\rho$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]: $P=\rho^{-1}(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})=\bigcup_i\rho^{-1}(D_+(T_i))=\bigcup_iD_+(T_i)_S$.

*(b): reduction to $h=\rho\circ g$.* Let $g:Y\to P$ and put $h=\rho\circ g:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, $D=D_+(T_i)$, $Y_i=g^{-1}(D_+(T_i)_S)=g^{-1}\rho^{-1}(D)=h^{-1}(D)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1) (twice), $\mathcal O_P(1)=\rho^*\mathcal O(1)$ and $g^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ are invertible ($\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] (i)). By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (2) there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $c:g^*\rho^*\mathcal O(1)\to h^*\mathcal O(1)$ with $c(g^*\rho^*s)=h^*s$; with $T_k=\rho^*T_k$ on $P$ this reads $c(g^*T_k)=h^*T_k$. Since the maps on sections of a composite of morphisms compose, $g^*(u_{j/i})=g^\sharp(\rho^\sharp(T_j/T_i))=h^\sharp(T_j/T_i)$ in $\mathcal O_Y(Y_i)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. As $c$ is an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear isomorphism, (b) for $g$ follows from (b'): $h^*T_i$ is a free generator of $h^*\mathcal O(1)$ over $Y_i$, and $h^*T_j|_{Y_i}=h^\sharp(T_j/T_i)\,h^*T_i|_{Y_i}$ (steps 4-6).

proof.text: *$h^*T_i$ is a free generator over $Y_i$.* $h^*\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible ([lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1)). By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] applied on $Y$ to $\mathcal L=h^*\mathcal O(1)$ and $s=h^*T_i$, the map $\mathcal O_{Y_s}\to\mathcal L|_{Y_s}$, $a\mapsto a\,s$, is an isomorphism, i.e. for every open $V\subseteq Y_s$ every $t\in\mathcal L(V)$ is $a\cdot s|_V$ for exactly one $a\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$. By step 4, $Y_s=Y_i$: this is the first assertion of (b').

proof.text: *The relation $h^*T_j=h^\sharp(T_j/T_i)\,h^*T_i$ on $Y_i$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] (iv), $T_j|_D=(T_j/T_i)\cdot T_i|_D$ in $\mathcal O(1)(D)$ with $T_j/T_i\in\Gamma(D,\mathcal O)$. The unit $\eta:\mathcal O(1)\to h_*h^*\mathcal O(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-modules, where $(h_*h^*\mathcal O(1))(D)=(h^*\mathcal O(1))(Y_i)$ is an $\mathcal O(D)$-module through $h^\sharp$, and it commutes with restriction; $\eta(T_k)=h^*T_k$. Applying $\eta_D$ to the identity gives $(h^*T_j)|_{Y_i}=h^\sharp(T_j/T_i)\cdot(h^*T_i)|_{Y_i}$, the second assertion of (b'). (Step 4 of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage] is the same computation for $\psi$.) With step 3 (transport along $c$) and step 1 (transport along $\theta$), (b) is proved.

proof.text: *(c): the open as a fibre product.* Let $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ be an affine open, $i\in n$, $D=D_+(T_i)$ and $W=D_+(T_i)_S\cap q^{-1}(S')=\rho^{-1}(D)\cap q^{-1}(S')$. $P=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with projections $q,\rho$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with $U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, $V=S'\subseteq S$, $W'=D\subseteq\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$), the canonical morphism $\iota:S'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}D\to P$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is an open immersion with image $q^{-1}(S')\cap\rho^{-1}(D)=W$, and $q\circ\iota$, $\rho\circ\iota$ are the two projections followed by the inclusions of $S'$, $D$.

*(c): the affine computation.* By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts] (ii), $D\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[U_j:j\in n\setminus\{i\}]$, the polynomial ring in the elements $U_j=T_j/T_i$ of $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O)$; and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map $\mathbf Z\to B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and there is only one ring map $\mathbf Z\to B$, so the maps of $S'$ and $D$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ are induced by the structure maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (base ring $\mathbf Z$, $A=R$, $B=\mathbf Z[U]$), $S'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}D\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[U])$ with projections $\operatorname{Spec}(r\mapsto r\otimes1)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(p\mapsto1\otimes p)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] ($A=\mathbf Z$), $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[U]\cong R[U]$ with $r\otimes1\mapsto r$, $1\otimes U_j\mapsto U_j$. With step 7, $\iota$ gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R[U]\cong W$ under which $q|_W:W\to S'$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the inclusion $R\to R[U]$ and $\rho|_W:W\to D$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\mathbf Z[U]\to R[U]$, $U_j\mapsto U_j$.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01JO / Lemma 01JR (fibre products of affine schemes: Spec A ×_{Spec R} Spec B = Spec(A ⊗_R B)); Constructions, Lemma 01NG for D_+(T_i) = Spec Z[T_j/T_i]

proof.text: *(c): conclusion.* By step 8, $W$ is affine. Taking global sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum] ($\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ induces $\varphi$ on global sections), the isomorphism of step 8 gives a ring isomorphism $\beta:R[U]\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_P)$ which is $R$-linear for the $R$-algebra structure of $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_P)$ through $q^\sharp:R=\Gamma(S',\mathcal O_S)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_P)$ (as $q|_W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to R[U])$), and sends $U_j$ to $\rho^\sharp(T_j/T_i)|_W=u_{j/i}|_W$ (as $\rho|_W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(U_j\mapsto U_j)$ and $U_j=T_j/T_i$ in $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O)$). An $R$-algebra map out of the polynomial ring $R[U_j:j\in n\setminus\{i\}]$ is determined by the images of the $U_j$, so $\beta$ is the map $U_j\mapsto u_{j/i}$ of (c), which is therefore an isomorphism.
